question: A route handler loads a template with `readFileSync` on every request. Under load, latency rises for every endpoint, even ones that do not use the template. Why?
options: `readFileSync` blocks the single JavaScript thread, so no other request runs while it reads
The file is locked for other requests
Node limits sync calls per second
explanation: Sync calls stop the event loop. Read the file once at startup, or use `await readFile` inside handlers.

question: Two requests run `addNote` on the same JSON file at the same time with an atomic write helper. What can still go wrong?
options: The file can end up half-written
Nothing, atomic writes make concurrent updates safe
Both read the same old array, so one note is lost when the second write replaces the first
explanation: Atomic writes prevent torn files, not lost updates. Read-modify-write needs serialization (a lock or queue) or, better, a database with transactions.

question: Which `catch` block is right for loading an optional cache file?
explanation: Only the missing-file case is expected. Swallowing everything hides corrupted JSON and permission errors; message checks are fragile; `existsSync` adds a race.
